title: [finding] a mail template hole whose formatter text is not one word (`{{ x | date-long }}`, `{{ x | currency :EUR }}`) passes every mail door and is printed verbatim, while the in-app dialect refuses it
body:
Filing gate: ① a declared rule with no judge, measured by in-flight work. The contract review on PR #27217 (#26948, record `6467428438`, should-fix S1) found this, and the #26948 dev measured it. Filed by `domain:spec` seat 1 · `os-support-ai` · session `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh`. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade yet: triage sets the lane and grade. The spec lane is suggested, working across formula, plugin-email and lint.

**Business reason.** Suppose a mail template author writes a formatter with a hyphen, a space before the argument, or two words: `{{ due | date-long }}`, `{{ amount | currency :EUR }}`, `{{ x | two words }}`. No door refuses it: not `os validate`, not `os lint`, not the `email_template` publish door. The email then goes out with the literal hole text `{{ due | date-long }}` in the body. The in-app template dialect refuses the same text at compile. Once #26948 lands, mail refuses an unknown one-word formatter by name, but non-word formatter text still gets through.

## Measured (#27217 head, merged with `main`)

- `@objectstack/formula` `mail-hole-grammar.ts`: when a hole's formatter part fails `FILTER_RE` / `WORD_RE`, `parseMailHole` returns `null`. Every rule in the `email-template-hole-grammar` union reads a parsed hole, so a `null` hole is never judged.
- In `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts`, a hole that does not parse is printed verbatim. That behaviour is pinned at `text-field-html-outlets.pin.test.ts:284`.
- The in-app dialect refuses the same text at compile (`invalid-template`).

## Wanted

- The mail hole grammar treats a hole that has a `|` whose formatter part does not parse as a refusal, not an unparsed hole. It names the hole and states the formatter shape: one word, with an optional `:argument`. This covers the lint rule, the publish door and the renderer (`TEMPLATE_INVALID`).
- Decide whether the verbatim print pinned at `text-field-html-outlets.pin.test.ts:284` is still correct for a hole that is not a formatter use, such as literal text that should stay printed. Pin the boundary either way.
- This is BREAKING for a stored template carrying such a hole: it is refused at its next publish and at render. ADR-0087 disposition: likely a D3 note, since a conversion cannot guess the intended formatter. Census the shipped templates first.

**Clause-②:** likely `no (narrowing)`. **Metadata-protocol:** likely `narrowed`. Land after PR #27217 (#26948), which edits the same grammar files.

## Dedupe

The open-issue titles were searched for "formatter", "mail hole", "parseMailHole" and "FILTER_RE". The only hit was PR #27217 itself. **New.**
